summary: Iter-24 verification of (a) Approval Workflows bug fix — Specific User/Specific Staff approver resolution + email-fallback self-heal + chain step validation on POST/PUT, and (b) Leave Allocation feature — leave-types lazy seed + CRUD, leave-balances allocate/list/my/PATCH, auto-deduction on approval with inclusive day-count. Backend: 23/23 pytest pass (test_iter24_leave_allocation.py). Frontend: /hr-settings 'Leave Allocation' tab loads, 11 leave-type cards render (5 defaults + test-created), btn-new-leave-type opens Add Type dialog, btn-allocate opens Allocate dialog with alloc-type+alloc-days fields; /hrms Apply Leave dialog now shows leave-type select with the placeholder hint 'Pick type (auto-deducts balance on approve)'. Critical end-to-end verified: 3-day leave Apr 10-12 with leave_type_id, when final-approved via kind=user chain, deducts exactly 3 days from the staff balance (used: 0→3, balance dropped by 3) — visible in the screenshot of HR Settings staff balances table.

design_issues.screen: Apply Leave & Add Type & Allocate dialogs
issues: Console warning: 'Missing Description or aria-describedby for DialogContent' on all 3 new dialogs — accessibility nit, non-blocking. Add DialogDescription to each shadcn Dialog for screen-reader support.

action_items: Optional a11y polish: add <DialogDescription> to LeaveAllocationTab's 3 dialogs (Type CRUD, Allocate, Adjust) and HRMS Apply Leave dialog to silence 'Missing aria-describedby' console warnings.
critical_code_review_comments: _resolve_step_user_ids for kind='user' returns [value] without checking that the user actually exists. If an admin deletes a user later, the chain dead-ends silently with a 403 on /approvals/act. _validate_chain_steps verifies user existence on save, but not on later GETs. Consider validating at resolution time too (or scheduled audit).

/api/leave-balances/allocate scope semantics: when staff_ids is non-empty AND center_id is also set, staff_ids wins and center_id is ignored. This is undocumented and could surprise admins. Either add a 400 if both are provided, or document the precedence in the API doc.

_deduct_leave_balance_on_approve recomputes balance = max(0, allocated - used) but never enforces 'used <= allocated' on insert/allocate. If admin uses delta_used to push used past allocated, allocated stays but balance pegs to 0 — fine, but it would be nice to warn the HR user.

GET /api/leave-balances for role='senior_manager' with no assigned_center_ids returns ALL balances (intentional per code comment), but for role='manager' or 'accountant' with no assigned_center_ids returns balances filtered by an empty $in list → empty result. Subtle role asymmetry worth a comment in code.

Leave types codes are uppercased on POST/PUT but not on the seeder (DEFAULT_LEAVE_TYPES). Verify DEFAULT_LEAVE_TYPES already uses uppercase codes (it does — CL/SL/PL/COMP/LWP — but a comment to prevent future regressions would help).

_count_leave_days uses datetime.fromisoformat which accepts both 'YYYY-MM-DD' and 'YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS' strings. If a leave is created with a datetime instead of date, the inclusive-count math still works because .date() is taken — good. But the field is documented as 'YYYY-MM-DD' only; consider explicit validation in LeaveIn.

context_for_next_testing_agent: Iter-24 added Leave Allocation feature + approval-chain staff/user fix. Key endpoints: GET /api/leave-types (lazy-seeds 5 defaults), POST/PUT/DELETE /api/leave-types (admin/hr); POST /api/leave-balances/allocate (modes: set|add; scope: staff_ids > center_id > all-staff); GET /api/leave-balances?staff_id=&year=&center_id=; GET /api/leave-balances/my; PATCH /api/leave-balances/{id} (delta_allocated, delta_used, remarks). LeaveIn now has optional leave_type_id — final-approve of a leave triggers _deduct_leave_balance_on_approve which uses inclusive day-count (Apr10-12 = 3 days). Approval chains: POST/PUT now run _validate_chain_steps — kind=staff requires staff.user_id OR staff.email matching a registered user (email-fallback auto-heals staff.user_id). kind=user requires the user to exist. For UI tests use data-testid: tab-leave-allocation, btn-new-leave-type, btn-allocate, lt-card-{code}, alloc-type, alloc-days, alloc-scope-{specific|center|all}, bal-row-{id}, btn-adjust-{id}, leave-type (in HRMS Apply Leave dialog). Pending-approvals item shape: {request_id, request_type, current_level, ...} — NOT 'id'.
rca of the issue: Iter-24 bug fix RCA: Original bug — POST /api/approval-chains accepted a step like {kind:'staff', value:<staff_id>} even when that staff had no user_id linked, causing /approvals/pending to silently return empty (the chain dead-ended at L1). Similarly kind='user' had no validation that the user existed. Fix introduced _validate_chain_steps (server.py:3026) called on POST (line 3080) and PUT (line 3105) that (a) rejects empty value with 400 'Level N: please choose a {kind} for the approver', (b) for kind=staff, if staff.user_id is missing, attempts email-fallback by matching staff.email → users.email (case-insensitive, regex-escaped); on match it auto-heals staff.user_id and saves; on no match returns 400 with staff name + remediation hint, (c) for kind=user verifies user existence. The runtime resolver _resolve_step_user_ids (server.py:2875) also has the same email-fallback so pre-existing broken chains self-heal on first /approvals/pending or /approvals/act call without admin intervention. Reproduction (passing as a test): create staff with email matching no user → POST chain with kind=staff,value=staff.id → 400. Create staff with email matching a registered user → POST → 200 + staff.user_id auto-populated. All 23 backend tests pass on the public preview URL.
